sources.name: pstack
sources.why: Cursor's in-house plugin: skills, commands and subagents shipped as one opinionated stack. Already the source of the vendored unslop skill.

sources.name: mattpocock-skills
sources.why: One person's skill set for TDD, diagnosis, domain modelling and writing for agents. Installed here as a plugin, so it can also be watched in use.

sources.name: anthropic-skills
sources.why: Anthropic's own skills, including skill-creator. The format's authors writing in the format — the closest thing to a spec for what a SKILL.md is supposed to be.

sources.name: codex-system-skills
sources.why: Codex's own bundled skills, already on disk. The only source that shows what the other harness expects of a skill; no fetch needed, read it in place.

candidates.name: superpowers
candidates.why: Jesse Vincent's plugin: brainstorm -> plan -> TDD pipeline with subagents, and skills that write skills. Prior art for a setup that is a system rather than a bag of tips.

candidates.name: humanlayer
candidates.why: The research -> plan -> implement command trio behind their context-engineering talk. Prior art for spending the context window deliberately, which is the constraint every long session hits.

candidates.name: hooks-mastery
candidates.why: Worked hook examples. Hooks are the one component type this repo has none of, and the only one that runs without asking the model nicely.

candidates.name: wshobson-agents
candidates.why: Dozens of role-play subagents. Proposed as a negative control: read it to see what description-matching looks like when it collapses, not to take anything.

reading.why: The harness authors on how they use it.
Why context budget, not model quality, is usually the limit.
Workflow versus agent, and when a subagent is the wrong answer.
Tool and description design — the same discipline a skill description needs.
